entities.summary:
Lysistratus was a Greek sculptor of the 4th century BC, brother of Lysippos. He is known for his realistic style and was the first sculptor to take impressions of human faces in plaster. According to Pliny the Elder, Lysistratus followed a strongly realistic line, which was a departure from the more idealized forms of ancient Greek sculpture. His innovations had a significant impact on the development of Western art.

The core of Lysistratus' significance lies in his contributions to the field of sculpture, particularly in the area of realism. His work was influential in shaping the course of Western art, and his techniques were adopted by later artists. Lysistratus' legacy can be seen in the works of later sculptors, such as Phidias and Praxiteles.

One of the most enduring legacies of Lysistratus is his innovative use of plaster casts to capture human likenesses. This technique, known as 'plaster casting,' allowed for greater accuracy and realism in sculptural representations. The impact of Lysistratus' work can be seen in the many plaster casts that remain today, a testament to his enduring influence on the art world.

In the world of art history, Lysistratus is often regarded as a key figure in the development of Western sculpture. His contributions to the field of realism had a profound impact on the course of art history, and his legacy continues to be felt today.
